items.heading: Most Benefits Content Is Written
items.text: Most benefits content is written for anyone, students and working professionals together, and lists the same general points: clearer decisions, better self-confidence, wider awareness of options. Those are real, but a student's actual situation adds three pressures that a general list does not address.

items.heading: The Strongest Available Research
items.text: The strongest available research on was not run only on students, but several parts of it speak directly to a student's academic decision, not just a general adult career choice.

items.heading: Not Every Provider Adds
items.text: Not every provider adds the same thing on top of a test result, this is what tends to matter for a stream, subject, or college decision specifically.

items.heading: A Student's Decision Runs Against
items.text: A student's decision runs against a calendar a working professional's does not, board exams, entrance-exam windows, and admission deadlines that close on a fixed date, not whenever the student feels ready.

items.heading: A Parent Is Almost Always
items.text: A parent is almost always part of approving the outcome, which changes what "benefit" means: a documented, checkable plan matters as much as the student's own conviction.

items.heading: Most Indian Students Can Name
items.text: Most Indian students can name a handful of careers out of the hundreds that realistically exist, the first benefit is simply widening that list before narrowing it.
